question: True or false: each neuron releases just one kind of chemical messenger from its endings?
answer: False. Many neurons release two or more: a fast transmitter such as glutamate or GABA alongside slower signalling peptides, and some dopamine neurons release glutamate. The one-transmitter idea misreads Dale's principle, which claimed only that a neuron releases the same messengers at every ending. One ending can hold small and large vesicles side by side.
move: Check what a famous rule literally says before quoting its nickname.
trap: Recalling the neat rule of one neuron, one transmitter.
source: Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science
reference: Kandel, Schwartz, Jessell, Siegelbaum & Hudspeth, Principles of Neural Science, 5th edition, McGraw-Hill, 2013
